findings.finding: The release will be the first company statement on what insurance covers for Prospector 5. Borr's May 2026 prospectus (section 7.9) says it buys hull-and-machinery cover for the whole fleet at each rig's 'agreed value', P&I covering death and injury of employees and third parties, pollution and wreck removal, excess umbrella liability, and loss-of-income cover for certain rigs. Since the 24 Oct sinking the stock has fallen about $1.2/share (about $350m of market cap on 309m shares), from about $4.5 to $3.30. A per-rig book value of roughly $100-200m (fleet PP&E spread over 29 rigs) is well below that, so the market is pricing liability beyond the hull loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior rig loss. The incident days themselves: -10.0% (2026-10-26) and -8.5% (2026-11-02, the day the fourth body was recovered and the 'halts operations' headlines ran), per baseline tape and MarketScreener headlines.
findings.why_not_priced: Every piece of coverage (TIKR 2026-10-26, Simply Wall St 2026-11-01, Panabee) says Borr has not disclosed what insurance covers. The market has priced the uncertainty: a market-cap loss larger than any plausible book value of one jack-up. If the insured-at-agreed-value language had been priced, the post-incident loss would be close to the deductible plus lost backlog, not about 24% of equity. Path to the multiple: removing the uninsured-liability tail is what the drawdown rests on, so this is not a below-the-line item without a path. Risks: a deductible, an exclusion (for example a punch-through during preload), a Gabonese government claim, or an impairment wording that reads as a loss.

Norve is idle until a mid-December start and Joro is on lower-value accommodation work. A softer Q4 activity guide and lower 2027 coverage are likely.

findings.finding: Peer Valaris (Q3 2026, released 2026-11-02): jackup contract drilling expenses fell 10% q/q, partly on lower war-risk insurance after longer-term policies were placed at lower rates. Its company-wide Middle East conflict hit to EBITDA fell from about $30m in Q2 to about $24m in Q3. Borr's Q2 carried $7.3m of higher insurance and fuel costs from the same conflict, so its Q3 cost line plausibly eased too. Valaris jackup revenue still fell 7% (one rig in the shipyard), and Valaris gave no outlook because of the Transocean merger.

findings.finding: Liquidity is not the question the rig loss raises. Liquidity was $473.6m at the end of Q2 2026, the super-senior RCF was upsized to $250m, and the Q2 refinancing pushed substantially all debt to 2032-2034 (secured notes due 2032/2034, $300m converts due 2033) with no significant maturities before 2032. findings.finding: Mexico counterparty credit risk: Pemex supplier debt was above US$20bn as of August 2026 (AMESPAC), with payments delayed as long as seven months to offshore service providers. Borr runs a large Mexico jack-up book (Galar and Gersemi extended with Pemex to 2030, plus a five-rig JV with its Mexican partner). It booked credit-loss provisions on a West African customer in both Q1 ($8.4m) and Q2 ($10.8m) 2026, so another receivables provision is a plausible miss source.
findings.link: Pemex is the end customer of Borr's Mexico rigs via its Mexican well-construction partner. The share of Borr revenue was not found.
